data.narrative: The student chose fail-fast errors with a stable envelope (code, message, request_id), proved 400/422/401/500 over ASGI, and kept stacks in logs only. BREAK injected PII into the 401 log line; FIX removed the header concat and kept secret/email redaction. They did not claim a live DB 500 from a wrong DATABASE_URL restart — /debug/error was the unexpected 500, and Postgres remains down.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose fail-fast for the client contract so a failed lookup is 404/503, not a guessed redirect, while analytics stays a logged side path.
dimension_scores.evidence: DECIDE A: never a guessed Location; 500 body is internal_error plus request_id, not a partial JSON resource.

dimension_scores.observation: Reproduced the PII log leak with a 401 plus an email header, then used the same request as the regression.
dimension_scores.evidence: Before: error_detail included pii=<email>. After: FIX_PII_IN_LOGS False and error_detail=Invalid API key only.

dimension_scores.observation: Client bodies have no stack; logs redact API keys, a sentinel, and email-shaped strings; 401 does not echo the presented key.
dimension_scores.evidence: SERVER_HAS_TRACE False; SENTINEL_IN_LOGS False for DO_NOT_LOG_ME_123; envelope message remains Invalid API key.

dimension_scores.observation: Logs already include request_id, route, status, duration_ms; 500s stay joinable via X-Request-ID without a DB restart.
dimension_scores.evidence: GET /debug/error returns request_id in JSON and header; logs contain the same request_id and stack_trace.

dimension_scores.observation: Named the error flow (raise -> handler -> envelope vs log) instead of only saying it was fixed.
dimension_scores.evidence: progress/system-design-module5-fix.md traces require_api_key HTTPException through http_exception_handler to error_payload.

strengths: Consistent envelope across 400, 422, 401, and 500 with request_id in body and header.
Closed a PII-in-logs bug with a same-request regression instead of only removing the line.
growth_areas: Add GET /ready to the error-envelope script so 503 service_unavailable is proven in the same harness (skipped here to avoid a 4s connect timeout).
data.recommendation: When Postgres is up, assert a DB-backed 503 envelope on /ready and confirm driver exceptions still cannot put a password into either the body or the log after redaction.

public_evidence.student_action: Mapped HTTPException, validation errors, and unhandled exceptions to error.code/message/request_id.
public_evidence.technical_detail: api/app/main.py error_payload plus handlers for HTTPException, RequestValidationError, and Exception; middleware 500 path uses the same shape.
public_evidence.proof: module05_error_verify.py: 400 validation_error, 422 validation_error, 500 internal_error with no Traceback in the body.
public_evidence.ability: Designs client-safe failure contracts that still join to logs.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the student can keep 2am debugging without turning a 500 into a disclosure.

public_evidence.student_action: Stopped copying request headers into error_detail and redacted secrets/sentinels/email-shaped strings in emit_log.
public_evidence.technical_detail: http_exception_handler logs only the stable message; redact_secrets runs on every emit_log string field.
public_evidence.proof: 401 with a sentinel API key: SENTINEL_IN_LOGS False. After FIX, the 401 log is error_detail=Invalid API key with no pii= field.
public_evidence.ability: Treats logs as a production surface that can leak PII.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Incident logs that contain emails or keys become a second breach; this work prevents that class.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: DECIDE A; 500/4xx return a generic envelope rather than partial resources.
X-Request-ID header matches error.request_id and the request_id log field on GET /debug/error.
401 handler briefly logged an email header; FIX removed it and verified the address was gone.

teaching_approaches.detail: Compared GET /debug/error JSON body to the log stack_trace on the same request_id.
